champion: Cerebellar variant of multiple system atrophy
ordered_diagnoses: Cerebellar variant of multiple system atrophy

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Unable to stop myoclonus of the palate with voluntary use of palatal musculature
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12

s4.champion: Cerebellar variant of multiple system atrophy

raw.champion: Cerebellar variant of multiple system atrophy
raw.rationale: The combination of progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction (implied by the progression of gait difficulty after cessation of alcohol use), bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI supports this diagnosis. The presence of palatal myoclonus also aligns with this condition.

rejected.label: Multiple system atrophy
rejected.why: While similar, the specific cerebellar variant better explains the predominant cerebellar symptoms and atrophy

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
rejected.why: Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal, and type 7 was not specifically tested but the clinical presentation and other findings point more towards a multiple system atrophy variant

rejected.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by palatal myoclonus but does not account for the broad range of other neurological symptoms and severe atrophy

rejected.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a combination of ataxia, myoclonus, and dementia, but the specific pattern of symptoms and the imaging findings in this case are more suggestive of a cerebellar variant of multiple system atrophy
